create_profiles.name: neokapi documentation
create_profiles.description: Academic, precise register for neokapi user-facing text: docs site, CLI help, UI copy, release notes. Explain what something is and what it does; let the facts stand without selling.

tone.guidelines: State capabilities plainly. Lead with the problem and the mechanism, not adjectives. Every claim must be checkable against the code or a generated artifact. One idea per sentence; short sentences over long ones. The reader is a developer or the person running the language work, not a prospect.

prohibited_patterns.description: Marketing superlatives and hype words

prohibited_patterns.regex: \b(production-proven|everything you need|localize at scale|just point and go)\b
prohibited_patterns.description: Brochure framing
Content memory is the store; brand is a coordinate on it, not a kind of memory
Retired positioning — say what the product does, not which axis it leads with
Retired positioning — kapi converges content; drafting is one step in the loop
Retired positioning — team framing belongs to the platform, not to kapi
Retired positioning — this is a content and language engine
Emoji in committed prose
Hardcoded counts that the code controls — name categories and link to the generated reference instead
"magic" as a claim about the product — state the mechanism; the technical sense (magic bytes, magic number) is not this rule
Extraction — not segmentation — produces blocks; segmentation is an opt-in overlay within a block
termbase: the store is the terms store, and its contents are terms (TBX, the ISO standard, keeps its name)
glossary: the store is the terms store (XLIFF 2.x's Glossary module keeps its name)
Say multilingual content, or language — and recast the sentence rather than substituting a word for "localize"
Say multilingual content, or language (the l10n-* make targets are developer-facing internals and are not this rule)
translation memory: say content memory
Voice is the mechanism — say voice profile. "Brand voice" belongs in prose about the common use case, never as the name of the thing

examples.before: kapi delivers powerful, seamless format support for everything you need.
examples.after: kapi reads and writes document, data and translation interchange formats.
examples.explanation: State the capability plainly; remove superlatives and brochure framing

examples.before: The translatable text is segmented into 42 blocks across 15+ formats.
examples.after: The text is extracted into blocks; see the formats reference for the supported formats.
examples.explanation: Neutral mechanism wording, extraction not segmentation, no hardcoded counts
Sentence case for headings; drop the sales tagline

nb.cultural_notes: Norwegian Bokmål. Address the reader as "du". Use established Norwegian software terminology where it exists (see the project's terms) and keep the academic, plain register — Norwegian technical prose tolerates anglicisms, but prefer the Norwegian term when the terms name one. Never translate product names (neokapi, kapi, kapi-desktop, Bowrain), CLI commands, flags, file formats, code identifiers, or file paths. Headings in sentence case. Compound nouns close up in Norwegian (innholdsbase, not "innholds base") — never leave an English noun pair half-translated.

put_concepts.definition: Frames the shared engine as translation-only; use neutral wording unless the context really is about translation

create_profiles.description: Register for Bowrain's user-facing text: landing, app UI, docs, and email. Addressed to the person accountable for content across a team, not to a developer reading a reference. Explain by contrast and state the outcome.

tone.guidelines: Lead with what changes for the reader, then the mechanism that makes it true. Explain by contrast when a distinction carries the point — a legal notice is not a help article. Address the reader as someone answerable for content quality, who has the problem already and does not need convincing it exists. Claims stay checkable: name what the product does, never how it feels to use. Sentences carry one idea.

nb.cultural_notes: Norwegian Bokmål. Address the reader as "du". Use established Norwegian software terminology where the terms store names one, and keep the plain, declarative register. Never translate product names (Bowrain, kapi, neokapi, kapi-desktop), CLI commands, flags, file formats, code identifiers, or file paths. Headings in sentence case. Compound nouns close up in Norwegian — never leave an English noun pair half-translated.

create_profiles.description: How a code comment in this repository reads.

tone.guidelines: A comment says what the code does and why, for the next person reading it. It describes the code as it is, never what it used to be, and leaves the history to git.

prohibited_patterns.description: An em dash; use a comma, a full stop or two sentences.
The past-habitual "used to"; describe what the code does.
A negation reveal ("is not X, it is Y"); state what it is.
A significance label; state the claim.
Temporary or open work; describe what the code does, and track the work elsewhere.
History; describe the code as it is.
